# Planner

Outline. Read `AGENTS.md` first; its hard limits aren't repeated here.

## Entry points

- habit's idea: grill it with `grilling` and `domain-modeling`, then choose the delivery
  shape below.
- An incoming issue: habit invokes `triage`. Its agent brief, plus the three ticket
  additions below, is that issue's contract once it reaches `ready-for-agent`.
- A foggy effort: habit invokes `wayfinder`; it rejoins here at `to-spec`.
- A direct request reaches a Builder, not a Planner (`builder.md`), unless the Builder
  hands it here because it outgrew one session.

## Delivery shape

- One Builder session can finish it: one ticket, no spec.
- Larger: `to-spec`, then `to-tickets`; one PR per ticket by default.
- Whole spec with `implement-spec` only when the tickets make sense only merged together
  and the combined diff stays reviewable. Never when any ticket is foreseen high.
- Keep a foreseen-high part in its own ticket; a high PR holds only the high part.
- habit approves the shape with the spec and tickets.

## Writing specs and tickets

- Spec: `to-spec`'s sections plus a Delivery section (ticket by ticket or whole spec, and
  why). After `to-tickets`, remove `ready-for-agent` from the spec.
- Ticket: `to-tickets`' body plus Skills (which skill covers which part), Verification (the
  commands the Builder runs and the Reviewer reruns, taken from `build.md`) and, only when
  the diff won't show it, Risk notes. No tier.
- End with one Builder start instruction for the first unblocked ticket, in two parts
  (`AGENTS.md`).

## Housekeeping

- A spec left open after its last ticket merged: close it the next time you touch it.
- Docs PRs for `GLOSSARY.md` and ADRs take the low path: follow `builder.md` from
  "Commit" to "Hand over", with the Planner in the Builder's place. Reference the spec or
  map; close no issue.

## Skills this role relies on

- habit invokes: `to-spec`, `to-tickets`, `triage`, `wayfinder`, `retro`.
- The session calls: `grilling`, `domain-modeling`, `research`, `prototype`,
  `codebase-design`; `writing-for-agents` when editing instructions.
